floor_history.headline: Recon s1: canonical island respell (func_800274BC form) lowered floor 33->30 with insn parity 144==144; full residual map banked; disc-copy survival is the frontier head.

s1 frontier head CLOSED: combine (not cse) folds the disc copy; an if/else-spelled LZCS guard makes it survive at zero insn cost, landing in $a0 (target's register) in the beqz delay slot. Floor still

frontier.hypothesis: Getting disc allocated to $a2/$6 (target) instead of $3 collapses most of the remaining 30 — it is the last head-of-cascade item now that the copy survives in $a0
frontier.mechanism: with the copy occupying $a0 (achieved by variant M), disc's own allocation is the only remaining occupancy difference at the beqz; slots 84-92 and the bltz at 96 are direct reads of it, and the downstream sqrt_val/t1/t2/result assignments re-run their tie-breaks under different occupancy
frontier.next_probe: this is an ALLOCATION question, not a structural one — read tmp/grind/func_8002D518/dumps/code6cac_b.lreg and .greg for the allocno covering disc (reg/v:SI 117) and for what currently occupies $6 across the beqz; check local-alloc's allocno priority/ordering against the copy's allocno. Only then propose a source change. Note that M's bltz reads the COPY ($4) where target reads disc ($a2) — check whether that cse canonicalisation is what pins disc low.

frontier.hypothesis: The 75-78 mult-shadow flip and its tail twin at 118-122 are reachable only by changing what reload produces, i.e. they will fall out of the disc-allocation fix rather than needing their own lever
frontier.mechanism: sched2 priorities (197=0x44 vs 200=0x18) are computed AFTER reload from hard-register dependencies; in target, dist_sq lands in $a1 (x1_sq's register), creating the WAR edge that forces its addu after slot 75. Different allocation, different priorities, different order.
frontier.next_probe: do NOT spend more source-reordering spellings here — A/H/K/C/G are all measured byte-identical and banked in rejected/. Re-measure the whole 154-slot alignment immediately after any allocation-moving change and attack this only if it survives.

frontier.hypothesis: M's bltz reading the copy ($4) where target reads disc ($a2) is a cse canon_reg choice that may itself be steerable, and steering it may be what fixes disc's register
frontier.mechanism: cse's canon_reg picks the quantity's representative register; in the M layout it chose the copy (132) for the guard branch (jump_insn 251). If the guard's operand is spelled so cse cannot equate it to the copy, the branch reads disc and disc's live range across the beqz changes shape.
frontier.next_probe: in the M form, spell the guard operand and the island input asymmetrically (guard on disc with island+srlv on ud, and the converse) and measure each as a complete file via run3.ps1; read .cse's canon_reg choice for jump_insn 251 in each. Two variants, cheap, and it directly tests the disc-register question.
